report.summary: Chunk 5 of 5 of canary.py: contains plan building, history I/O, comparison logic, and rendering. All docstring claims checked.

handoff.purpose: Plan building, history I/O, comparison logic, and rendering.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history, skips unreadable lines.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends probe result records to history file, creates parent dirs.

symbols.name: compare_to_history
symbols.note: Computes Comparison from a ProbeResult and history list.

symbols.name: render_table
symbols.note: Renders a compact human table of canary run results.

symbols.name: _VERDICT
symbols.note: Maps status strings to display strings.

claims.text: A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how --live becomes a surprise. Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: The claim about naming a seat being pure is not verifiable from this chunk; it references behavior of live_egress_lanes defined elsewhere.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: load_history catches JSON decode errors and skips non-dict, wrong schema, unknown status lines.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: load_history catches ValueError/TypeError from json.loads, so a truncated line is skipped.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: Lines failing json.loads or non-dict or wrong schema are skipped; loop continues.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: append_history opens file in append mode, creates parent dirs, never truncates.

claims.text: previously_passed is 'this exact vendor+model+probe has an ok on record'. That is what makes regressed mean 'it used to work and now it does not'.
claims.why: previously_passed is bool(oks) where oks are history entries with status 'ok' matching vendor, model, probe.

claims.text: An unavailable result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: regressed is True only if previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; 'unavailable' is not in FAILING_STATUSES (assumed, not shown but implied by logic).

claims.text: Latency and pass-rate against the trailing history for this triple.
claims.why: Function computes median latency and pass rate from prior matching entries.

claims.text: Compact human table: vendor, model, probe verdict, latency, vs median.
claims.why: render_table produces a table with those columns.

observations.what: The `live_seats` key in the returned dict is computed via `list(live_egress_lanes(lanes))` but the comment says 'Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.' This function is not defined in this chunk, but assuming it returns lane identities, the claim is plausible.
In `compare_to_history`, the variable `asked` is computed but only used for `prior_pass_rate`. It filters out 'unavailable' statuses, consistent with the docstring claim.

In `render_table`, the `detail` field uses `r.failed_check or r.reason`. If both are empty strings, detail will be an empty string, which is joined into the flags list. This is harmless but could produce an extra space.
